## The question

[triple integral- plane/cone](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2806084/triple-integral-plane-cone), asked by [kenobe](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/457841/kenobe) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-06-03; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Currently I am working on this problem that requires me to calculate this triple integral when I am given cone/plane intersection. The issue is that integrals in both cases (when using spherical and cylindrical coordinates) lead to, even more, complicated ones. Only hints required. Thank You.
> [![enter image description here][q-1]][q-1]
>
> >Calculate $$\int \int \int_E \sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}\space dV$$
>
> where $E$ is the is region bound by the plane $z=3$ and the cone $z=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$
>
>   [q-1]: ea5jL.jpg
:::

In cylindrical coordinates, the cone has equation $z=r$; it intersects the plane in a circle of radius $3$.  So the integral is equal to
$$\int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^3 \int_r^3 \sqrt{r^2+z^2}r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta
    = 2\pi \int_0^3 \int_r^3 \sqrt{r^2+z^2}r\,dz\,dr$$
As written the integral on the right needs a trigonometric substitution; it would be easier to rearrange the limits:
$$2\pi \int_0^3 \int_r^3 \sqrt{r^2+z^2}r\,dz\,dr
    = 2\pi \int_0^3 \int_0^z \sqrt{r^2+z^2}r\,dr\,dz$$
Can you take it from there?
